Traditional Mole Poblano

Served at: Dia de los Muertos

Serves 6Prep 30 minCook 2 hours

Mole Poblano is a rich, complex sauce made with a blend of chiles, spices, chocolate, and nuts, traditionally served over turkey or chicken during Día de los Muertos celebrations in Mexico. This dish honors ancestors by bringing families together to share food that symbolizes the blending of indigenous and Spanish cultures.

Ingredients

  • 4 dried ancho chiles, stemmed and seeded
  • 4 dried pasilla chiles, stemmed and seeded
  • 2 dried mulato chiles, stemmed and seeded
  • 1/4 cup sesame seeds (35 g)
  • 1/4 cup almonds (35 g)
  • 1/4 cup peanuts (35 g)
  • 1 corn tortilla, torn into pieces
  • 2 slices white bread, torn into pieces
  • 1 medium onion, chopped
  • 3 cloves garlic, minced
  • 1/2 teaspoon ground cinnamon
  • 1/4 teaspoon ground cloves
  • 1/4 teaspoon ground allspice
  • 1/2 teaspoon dried thyme
  • 1/4 cup raisins (40 g)
  • 1 ounce Mexican chocolate or bittersweet chocolate, chopped
  • 4 cups chicken broth (960 ml)
  • 2 tablespoons vegetable oil
  • Salt to taste
  • Cooked chicken or turkey, for serving

Method

  1. Toast the dried chiles in a dry skillet over medium heat for about 1-2 minutes until fragrant, being careful not to burn them.
  2. Place the toasted chiles in a bowl and cover with hot water. Let them soak for 20 minutes until softened, then drain and set aside.
  3. In the same skillet, toast the sesame seeds, almonds, and peanuts until golden and fragrant. Remove and set aside.
  4. Toast the tortilla pieces and bread slices in the skillet until crisp and browned. Set aside.
  5. In the skillet, heat 1 tablespoon of vegetable oil and sauté the chopped onion and garlic until translucent.
  6. In a blender, combine the softened chiles, toasted nuts and seeds, tortilla and bread pieces, sautéed onion and garlic, cinnamon, cloves, allspice, thyme, raisins, and chocolate. Add 2 cups of chicken broth and blend until smooth.
  7. Heat the remaining 1 tablespoon of oil in a large pot over medium heat. Pour in the blended sauce and cook, stirring frequently, for about 10 minutes.
  8. Add the remaining 2 cups of chicken broth to the pot. Simmer the mole sauce gently for 1 to 1.5 hours, stirring occasionally to prevent sticking.
  9. Season the mole with salt to taste. Serve hot over cooked chicken or turkey, garnished with additional sesame seeds if desired.

Tips

  • For a smoother mole, strain the sauce through a fine mesh sieve before simmering.
  • Adjust the number of chiles to control the heat level to your preference.
  • Mole can be made in advance and tastes even better the next day as flavors meld.
